ev.q: In 2020, 25.7% of adults aged ≥18 years with disability had diagnosed diabetes compared with 7.7% of those without disability.
adults aged 18–44 years (8.3% versus 2.2%), 45–64 years (25.3% versus 9.9%), and ≥65 years (34.2% versus 17.8%)
For each age group, those with disability were more likely to have diabetes
Estimates are based on household interviews of a sample of the civilian, noninstitutionalized U.S. population.

methods_quotes.q: * With 95% CIs indicated with error bars.
Adults who responded “a lot of difficulty” or “cannot do at all” to at least one domain were classified with disability.
